reading: CAMP test: an arrowhead of enhanced hemolysis where the isolate’s streak meets the Staphylococcus aureus β-lysin streak.
sourceCaption: Group B streptococcus, CAMP-positive (CDC teaching plate).

reading: Gram stain: numerous very small Gram-negative coccobacilli.
Gram stain: slender Gram-positive rods, singly and in short chains, some longer filaments.
credit: CDC / R. E. Weaver, MD, PhD

reading: Blood agar, 48 h: tiny, translucent, pinpoint colonies.
Gram stain: Gram-positive coccobacilli and short rods (coryneform).
credit: CDC / Regina Linder: Hunter College, New York, New York, USA

reading: Blood agar: moist, glistening colonies along the streak; no hemolysis.
The pen at the farm.
Gram stain: short Gram-positive rods, singly and in short chains.
sourceCaption: Listeria monocytogenes, Gram stain of a slant culture.

reading: Motility medium: growth spreading out from the stab line (right) compared with a non-motile control (left).
sourceCaption: Motility medium, non-motile and motile reactions (CDC teaching tubes).

reading: Gram stain: large, blunt-ended, boxcar-shaped Gram-positive rods; no spores seen.
sourceCaption: Clostridium perfringens type A, Gram stain, 956×.

reading: Egg-yolk half-antitoxin plate: opacity around colonies on the untreated half, suppressed where antitoxin was spread.
Sulfite-polymyxin-sulfadiazine (SPS) agar, anaerobic: dark colonies.
Gram stain: very small, faintly staining Gram-negative coccobacilli.
Sheep blood agar, close view: tiny, smooth, non-hemolytic colonies.
sourceCaption: Brucella suis on sheep blood agar, 24 h, 5×.
credit: CDC / Todd Parker, Ph.D., Assoc Director for Laboratory Science, Div of Preparedness and Emerging Infections at CDC

reading: Gram stain: slender, curved Gram-negative rods — commas, S-shapes and “gull wings.”
Skirrow selective blood agar, 42 °C microaerobic: small, round, grey colonies.
Trypticase soy agar: concentric waves of swarming growth, with a line where two strains meet (Dienes reaction).
sourceCaption: Proteus mirabilis, swarming and Dienes reaction.

reading: TSI: alkaline (red) slant, acid butt, heavy blackening from H₂S.
sourceCaption: TSI reaction of Proteus sp., H₂S-positive.

reading: TSI: acid (yellow) slant and butt, with gas splitting the agar; no H₂S.
sourceCaption: TSI reaction of Escherichia coli with gas.

reading: Gram stain: straight, slender Gram-negative rods.
Blood agar: spreading, irregular colonies.
Gram stain: lancet-shaped Gram-positive diplococci.
Blood agar with gentamicin, CO₂: small alpha-hemolytic colonies, several with collapsed “draughtsman” centers.
sourceCaption: Streptococcus pneumoniae colonies on blood agar.

reading: Optochin disks: a clear zone around the disk for your isolate (left); growth up to the disk for the control (right).
sourceCaption: Optochin test: S. pneumoniae sensitive (left), viridans streptococcus resistant (right).

reading: Gram stain: large Gram-positive rods in short chains.
Sheep blood agar, 24 h: large, flat, grey, slightly granular colonies with wide hemolysis.
sourceCaption: Bacillus cereus on sheep blood agar.
credit: CDC / Amanda Moore, MT; Todd Parker, PhD; Audra Marsh (photo: Pete Seidel)

reading: Hektoen enteric agar: small colonies on a blue-green background.
sourceCaption: Yersinia enterocolitica on Hektoen enteric agar.

reading: Serum, about 2 hours at 37 °C: yeast cells sending out slender germ tubes without constriction at the origin.
Cornmeal agar, 48 h: pseudohyphae bearing round, thick-walled chlamydospores.
sourceCaption: Candida albicans chlamydospores on cornmeal agar.

reading: Colonies on fungal medium: velvety to powdery, grey-green, with paler margins.
Tease mount, lactophenol cotton blue: a conidial head — a flask-shaped vesicle with phialides on its upper part, and columns of conidia.
Lung, PAS stain: hyphae and fruiting heads growing within an air space.
sourceCaption: Pulmonary aspergillosis in a sulphur-crested cockatoo, PAS, 600×.

reading: Gram stain: Gram-negative rods.
TSI: alkaline (red) slant, acid butt, blackened by H₂S.
sourceCaption: TSI reaction of an H₂S-positive Salmonella.

reading: TCBS agar: green colonies (sucrose not fermented).
Gram stain: small Gram-negative rods and coccobacilli.
